cards.explanation: The answer is the Book of the Law. Hilkiah the priest finds the Book of the Law of the LORD while the money is being brought out. Somebody went in to carry money out and came out holding Scripture. That's the best surprise anybody has ever found during repair work, friends. Everything after this hangs on that book.

The answer is Moses. The text says the book was given by Moses, Israel's leader, so this is the Book of the Law of the LORD that came through him. This isn't some random scroll that rolled out from behind a shelf. It's the real Law, and it was found in the house of the LORD.

The answer is that the money was paid to the supervisors and workers. Shaphan the scribe tells the king the money found in the house of the LORD has been paid out and put into the hands of the supervisors and workers. He says the servants are doing all that has been placed in their hands (2 Chronicles 34:16). Good report, friends, and then he gets to the book.

The answer is True. After Shaphan tells the king that Hilkiah has given him a book, he reads it in the presence of the king. So Josiah doesn't just hear about the book. He hears it read right there in front of him.

The answer is tore. When the king heard the words of the Law, he tore his clothes. Later the LORD says Josiah's heart was tender, and that he humbled himself, tore his clothes and wept before Him (2 Chronicles 34:27). I think those words hit him hard, friends.

The answer is to inquire of the LORD about the book. Josiah tells them, “Go and inquire of the LORD for me…” That's concerning the words in the book that has been found. He sends the men to ask the LORD about it, which tells you how seriously the king takes what he just heard.

The answer is False. Josiah says, “Go and inquire of the LORD for me and for those remaining in Israel and Judah…” He includes himself, and he also includes the people still in Israel and Judah. The king isn't asking only for his own sake.

The answer is that their fathers did not keep the LORD's word. Josiah says it's “…because our fathers have not kept the word of the LORD by doing all that is written in this book.” He's looking at what the book says and comparing it with what was done. He doesn't blame the paint or the roof. He names the word of the LORD that wasn't kept.

The answer is Huldah the prophetess. Hilkiah and the king's men go and speak to Huldah, the wife of Shallum. She lived in Jerusalem, and the LORD gives her the message for the king. She's the one they find with a word from Him.

The answer is calamity. The LORD says, “I am about to bring calamity on this place and on its people…” It's a hard message, and Huldah doesn't soften it. The king asked to hear from the LORD, and this is what comes back.

The answer is True. The LORD says the calamity will come “…according to all the curses written in the book that has been read in the presence of the king of Judah…” So what He says lines up with what's written in the book. The book Josiah heard is the same one Huldah's message points to.

The answer is that they forsook Him and burned incense to other gods. The LORD says it's “…because they have forsaken Me and burned incense to other gods…” The reason comes straight from Him, and He doesn't leave it vague. They turned away from Him and offered incense to other gods. That's the reason given, friends.

The answer is tender. The LORD says, “…because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before God when you heard His words…” A tender heart is one that can still be moved. Josiah heard the words and took them to heart. That's what the LORD notices about him.

The answer is True. The LORD says Josiah has humbled himself before Him, torn his clothes and “…wept before Me…” Then He says, “…I have heard you…” So the king's tears didn't go unnoticed. This is a sweet moment in a heavy chapter, friends.

The answer is that his eyes won't see all the calamity. The LORD says, “Your eyes will not see all the calamity that I will bring on this place and on its people.” He also says Josiah will be gathered to his grave in peace. This promise comes because Josiah humbled himself. The LORD heard him, and He answers.

The answer is that he reads them all the words of the book. In their hearing, Josiah reads all the words of the Book of the Covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD. Everyone is there, great and small, priests and Levites too. The whole crowd gets to hear it, not just the king.

The answer is True. The text says Josiah read all the words of the Book of the Covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD. It's the same book Hilkiah found, which earlier is called the Book of the Law. Same book, and it carries both names, friends.

The answer is to follow the LORD and keep His commandments. Josiah makes a covenant “…to follow the LORD and to keep His commandments, decrees, and statutes with all his heart and all his soul…” That's a full-hearted promise, not a half one. He also promises to carry out the words of the covenant written in the book. He heard the book, and now he's committing to it.

The answer is that they take a stand in agreement to it. Josiah has everyone in Jerusalem and Benjamin take a stand in agreement to the covenant. So the promise isn't only the king's. The people stand with him, and then all the people of Jerusalem carry out the covenant of God.

The answer is False. The text says, “Throughout his reign they did not turn aside from following the LORD, the God of their fathers.” So during Josiah's reign, the people kept following Him. After such a hard message, that's a bright line, friends.
